newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia metal official sees '97 platinum sales flat.
newsitem.headline: Russia metal official sees '97 platinum sales flat.

text.p: A senior Russian precious metals official said on Tuesday that Russia would probably not increase exports of platinum and palladium in 1997.

Asked if sales of both metals would rise, Yuri Kotlyar, acting head of the disbanded State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones (Komdragmet), said: "I doubt it -- the market situation is just not very good."
Kotlyar is at his post until December, after which he will join, and possibly head, a Finance Ministry body that will take over Komdragmet's functions, including exports.
Kotlyar declined to provide figures on Russian metals reserves, which are a closely guarded state secret.
He said that under recent presidential decrees reorganising the precious metals and stones industries, production issues would be handled by the Industry Ministry.

The Finance Ministry body replacing Komdragmet will be responsible for operations with precious metals and stones from strategic state reserves and will store and independently conduct operations with materials, including stocking and destocking reserves.
Johnson Matthey's Platinum 1996 Interim Review, published this month, said Russia would ship about 1.10 million ounces of platinum in 1996, down 180,000 ounces year-on-year.
The review said Russian shipments of palladium would fall to 3.8 million ounces this year from 4.2 million ounces in 1995.
